premises: High configurational entropy in multi-element alloys stabilizes a single solid-solution phase against phase separation or intermetallic formation.
Increasing the number of elements innately promotes a more random atomic arrangement in nanoparticles, regardless of element interactions.
Limited atomic mobility during synthesis (e.g., solid-state precursor reduction) is a key condition for entropy-driven randomization to dominate.
